name: GZA
sources: Sweetwater — the gear behind Wu-Tang Clan's Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers)
notes: The most austere model on this axis, and every number in it is a superlative the research states outright. "Slowest Wu tempi" gives an 82–92 band centred at 86. "Lowest note density in the lane" gives `melody.densityPerBar` 1–3. "A single sustained organ/string tone as the entire harmonic content" gives `timbreHint` `church_organ` and `impliedByRiff`. "Dissonant seconds when two fragments overlap" gives `halfStepDissonance` 0.26. "Hats often omitted entirely" gives a non-continuous hat block, and "velocity variation minimal" gives `velocityVar` 0.05. The `snareRoll` numbers are the extreme end of this batch's spread — `gapProb` 0.65, `descendProb` 0.05, `rampJitter` 2 — because a fill on these records is nearly not there. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick`, not a held note, and that is an engine limit rather than a reading of the record.** "Deep sustained sub, tonic-only... its only movement is the kick" is the most literal `mirror_kick` description in the whole section, and `followRootsProb` 0.98 keeps it on the tonic; `reese_sustain` is refused because it emits one note per chord and saturates. ⚠ The `i–iv` family is INFERRED and carries the lowest weight the model has — the research names static `i` only. It exists because the bass needs more than one reachable root and the generated chord part still owes a producer 55 distinct outputs over 200 seeds; it is the first thing to delete if this ever sounds busier than the records. ⚠ `hihat.fillDensity` is 0.28 rather than 0 because a model that declares a hat block owes every seed a hat — the research's "omitted entirely" is honoured as far as the engine allows and no further. ⚠ `medium` because the research rates it high-medium: the RZA production idiom is documented, the tempo band is catalog-level. ⚠ **The bass pool was widened after `bass.rs` measured it at 0.927 distinct against a floor of 0.95.** It was authored with NO passing tones, followRootsProb 0.98, anticipationProb 0.04 over register [22,40] — a faithful description of a sample-loop bass, and one that leaves a seed nothing to vary but root and octave. Now ["P5"], root lock 0.9, anticipation 0.18, register [22,44]. The line is still overwhelmingly root-on-kick; what changed is how many different records it can be, not how busy any one of them is. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 44 to 41 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 42 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 3. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 905 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.45. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [2,1,4], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 978/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, arp, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like.
